correctness.rationale: Connectivity and nested neighborhoods give a vertex universal to the opposite shore on each side, so labeling such a pair 3 is feasible. In any total double Roman function the positive support is nonempty and meets both sides. If both sides have a zero, defending it requires at least 3 weight from the opposite side; total weight at most 6 means exactly one 3 per side. Totality makes them adjacent, and the zero conditions give adjacency to every other vertex on their opposite sides. If just one side has zeros, the all-positive side needs at least 5 weight: defending the zero adds at least 2 above the all-positive baseline, whether using one 3 or two 2s. Thus the other side cannot contribute at least 2 at weight at most 6. But if it contributes only 1, every vertex on the all-positive side needs label at least 2, giving total weight at least 7. With neither side containing a zero, weight at most 6 would make all vertices 1, impossible. Therefore the product count follows, as does uniqueness on the half graph. The argument actually needs only both side sizes at least 3 and nonempty opposite-universal classes, rather than the chain ordering itself.
residual_risks: Finite support enumeration does not extend the theorem to small shores. The all-positive-side lower bound of 5 is also attained by the pattern 2,2,1 if both 2s neighbor the zero; the frozen proof needs only the bound, not uniqueness of the cheapest pattern.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the classification and product count of all total-double-Roman optima over the general chain family with both sides of size at least 3. Do not claim priority for scalar chain optimization or for the half-graph corollary. The indexed half-graph [2]-Roman result at k=2 is the non-total double Roman classification and really does imply the frozen uniqueness on that subfamily. Another indexed result has the same universal-pair supports with labels 2 for quasi-total Roman domination, a different constraint and weight. The exact 2021 total-double-Roman chain algorithm is materially relevant, but the indexed material gives optimization and a chain-graph case discussion, not all optimizers; lawful retrieval did not resolve its full coverage.
residual_risks: The full algorithmic chapter could contain an unverified scalar formula, proof revealing equality structure, or additional overlap. Its inaccessibility is not evidence against that possibility.
Priority and the existence of other equivalent general-chain counts are not settled by these bounded checks.

value.rationale: The claim identifies every minimum feasible labeling on a basic nested-neighborhood bipartite class. The product counts the optima and identifies precisely when they are unique; the correspondence depends only on the opposite-universal classes and survives beyond chains. This is useful information distinct from running a scalar optimizer, and does not rest on the overlapping half-graph example.
residual_risks: No classification for a shore of size 1 or 2 or for graphs without an opposite-universal pair is claimed.
